chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Wahb, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The deposit (Arbun) is not valid except if it is cash from the price.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Faithful, referring to Imam Ali)
key_terms.عَرَبُون: Arbun (a non-refundable deposit paid in advance in a sale contract)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of a cash deposit (Arbun) in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the chain of Shaykh al-Kulayni, clarifies the validity of 'Arbun' (earnest money) by restricting it to cash payment, thereby preventing ambiguity (gharar) in trade contracts. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on liquidity and certainty in financial transactions, distinguishing it from other forms of pre-payment that might involve uncertainty regarding the nature of the asset. It underscores the practical application of prophetic traditions in ensuring fairness and clarity in commercial dealings.
